events.text: The first revelation at the cave of Hira

easy.explain: Revelation began around 610 CE. Makkah was entered peacefully twenty years later, in 8 AH.
Masjid Quba was built on arrival in Madinah at the very start of the Madinan period. The Farewell Pilgrimage came nine years later, shortly before the Prophet's passing.

events.text: The Prophet ﷺ receives his first revelation
The Prophet ﷺ passes away in Madinah

easy.explain: Around twenty-two years separate the first revelation from the Prophet's passing in Madinah.

events.text: The caliphate of Uthman ibn Affan begins

easy.explain: Badr was fought in the second year after the Hijrah; Uthman became caliph twenty-one years later.
A group of Muslims first sought refuge in Abyssinia around 615 CE, some seven years before the migration to Madinah.

events.text: The birth of the Prophet ﷺ

easy.explain: The Prophet ﷺ was around fifty-two at the time of the Hijrah.

events.text: The caliphate of Abu Bakr begins

easy.explain: Hudaybiyyah came five years before the Prophet's passing and the accession of Abu Bakr.
The Year of the Elephant is traditionally placed around the Prophet's birth, some fifty-four years before Badr.
Around seventeen years passed between the start of public preaching in Makkah and the city's peaceful conquest.

events.text: The change of qiblah to the Ka'bah

easy.explain: The qiblah was changed early in the Madinan period; Tabuk was the last major expedition, seven years later.

medium.explain: Roughly three years of private calling preceded public preaching, and persecution soon after led a group to seek refuge in Abyssinia.

events.text: The change of qiblah to the Ka'bah

medium.explain: The qiblah was changed in the second year after the Hijrah, shortly before the Battle of Badr in Ramadan of that year.
Uhud, then the siege at Khandaq two years later, then the truce at Hudaybiyyah the year after that.
Khaybar followed within a year of the truce at Hudaybiyyah, and Makkah was entered the year after.
The final three years: the conquest of Makkah, the difficult expedition to Tabuk, and the Farewell Pilgrimage.
Umar led for about ten years, Uthman for about twelve, and Ali from 35 AH.

events.text: The birth of the Prophet ﷺ

medium.explain: The Prophet ﷺ was about forty at the first revelation and about fifty-two at the Hijrah.
After the loss of Khadijah and Abu Talib, the pledges given by the people of Yathrib opened the way for the migration.
All three fall within 8 AH: Mu'tah earlier in the year, then the conquest of Makkah in Ramadan, then Hunayn very soon afterwards.

events.text: The compilation of the Qur'an under Abu Bakr
The standardisation of copies under Uthman

medium.explain: The written collection was gathered under Abu Bakr, standard copies were distributed under Uthman, and Ali's caliphate followed.

hard.explain: The Makkan period in sequence, from the first revelation to the migration twelve years later.
The early Madinan years. The qiblah changed shortly before Badr, with Uhud the following year and the siege at Khandaq two years after that.
These years run close together. Khaybar came soon after the truce at Hudaybiyyah, and Mu'tah preceded the conquest of Makkah within the same year, 8 AH.
Hunayn followed the conquest within weeks. Tabuk and the Year of Delegations both fall in 9 AH, with the Farewell Pilgrimage the following year.

events.text: The caliphate of Abu Bakr begins
The caliphate of Hasan ibn Ali

hard.explain: The Rashidun period in order, concluding with the brief caliphate of Hasan ibn Ali before he ceded authority.

events.text: The birth of the Prophet ﷺ
The rebuilding of the Ka'bah by the Quraysh

hard.explain: The Prophet ﷺ was about thirty-five when the Quraysh rebuilt the Ka'bah and he settled the dispute over the Black Stone, about forty at the first revelation, and about fifty at the Isra and Mi'raj.
The founders of the four schools in order, followed by al-Bukhari, who was a student of the generation after Ahmad ibn Hanbal.
The compilers of five of the six books died within about twenty years of each other. Al-Nasa'i, who died in 915 CE, outlived them all.

The final Makkan years, from the loss of Khadijah and Abu Talib through the rejection at Ta'if and the night journey, to the pledge that enabled the migration. Precise dating of several of these is debated among historians.

events.text: The performance of the delayed Umrah

hard.explain: The truce at Hudaybiyyah freed the Muslims to send envoys to neighbouring rulers and to turn to Khaybar, and allowed the Umrah postponed the previous year to be performed in 7 AH.
